headline: McDavid's opening point streak reaches 23, ties Gretzky

top.headline: McDavid's opening point streak reaches 23, ties Gretzky
top.summary: Connor McDavid had a goal and an assist in Edmonton's 5-2 win at Florida. His 23-game streak to open the season ties Wayne Gretzky's 1988-89 run for the fourth-longest in NHL history. The Oilers (17-3-3) have won six straight.

top.headline: Pistons end Spurs' 12-game win streak
top.summary: Detroit won 105-93 in San Antonio behind 27 points from Cade Cunningham and 14 points, 12 assists, 9 rebounds and 5 steals from Ausar Thompson. The Spurs fall to 12-3 and had not lost since Oct. 23. Rookie Dylan Harper left late with an injury; his status is unclear.

top.headline: Bednar, Jeffers accept qualifying offers; five decline
top.summary: David Bednar stays with the Yankees and Ryan Jeffers with the Twins on one-year, $23.15M qualifying offers. Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki, Brandon Lowe, Trevor Rogers and Adrian Morejon declined and hit the market. Teams that sign them give up draft picks, with a possible lockout two weeks away.

leagues.name: NFL
leagues.summary: Raiders-Browns flexed to Sunday night; Texans lose Al-Shaair before Thursday's game

stories.headline: Raiders-Browns flexed to Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: The NFL moved the Week 12 Raiders-Browns game to NBC on Nov. 29 at 8:20 p.m. ET. Patriots-Chargers, first slotted for prime time, moves to 4:05 p.m. on CBS. The AP noted that flexing a game during Thanksgiving week is rare.

stories.headline: Texans put Al-Shaair on IR before Thursday game
stories.summary: Houston placed LB Azeez Al-Shaair on injured reserve after groin surgery; he'll miss at least four games. Henry To'oTo'o takes over his role, including the green dot, for Thursday's game against the Colts.

stories.headline: Mayfield's status for Detroit in doubt
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield has a lower leg injury and has been in and out of a walking boot during the Buccaneers' bye. It isn't expected to be long-term, but he may not be ready for Sunday at Detroit. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels would start again if he can't go.

stories.headline: Jets' Geno Smith uncertain for Chargers game
stories.summary: Geno Smith had imaging on his left ankle after leaving the 31-12 loss to Buffalo. Rookie Cade Klubnik would start if he can't. The Jets are 2-8, have lost five straight and have gone nine quarters without a touchdown.

leagues.summary: Pistons snap the Spurs' 12-game streak; Grimes drops 47 as the Lakers win a ninth straight

stories.headline: Pistons end Spurs' 12-game win streak
stories.summary: Detroit won 105-93 in San Antonio behind 27 points from Cade Cunningham and 14 points, 12 assists, 9 rebounds and 5 steals from Ausar Thompson. The Spurs fall to 12-3 and had not lost since Oct. 23. Rookie Dylan Harper left late with an injury; his status is unclear.

stories.headline: Grimes scores career-high 47 as Lakers win ninth straight
stories.summary: Quentin Grimes made 10 of 14 threes, including one late in regulation to force overtime, in a 118-114 win over Charlotte. Luka Doncic added 36, his 11th straight game with at least 30. The Hornets have lost nine of 10.

stories.headline: Sensabaugh scores 40 as Jazz rout Clippers
stories.summary: Brice Sensabaugh scored 40 with 11 rebounds on 16-of-21 shooting, 8 of 11 from three, in a 132-107 win in Los Angeles. Keyonte George added 30 points and 11 assists for a short-handed Utah team.

stories.headline: McDaniels layup with 2.6 seconds left beats Blazers again
stories.summary: A late steal set up Jaden McDaniels' go-ahead layup and Trey Lyles blocked Damian Lillard's last shot in Minnesota's 106-105 win. Ayo Dosunmu scored a season-high 30. The Wolves beat Portland for the second straight night.

stories.headline: Brunson's late four-point play seals Knicks' win in Toronto
stories.summary: Jalen Brunson scored 31 in a 111-102 win that moves New York to 8-6. Karl-Anthony Towns had 16 and 16 for his 14th straight double-double to open the season, a franchise record. The Knicks have beaten Toronto 14 straight times.

leagues.name: NHL
leagues.summary: McDavid ties Gretzky with a 23-game opening point streak; Gauthier's goal streak hits 10; Bedard hurt

stories.headline: McDavid's opening point streak reaches 23, ties Gretzky
stories.summary: Connor McDavid had a goal and an assist in Edmonton's 5-2 win at Florida. His 23-game streak to open the season ties Wayne Gretzky's 1988-89 run for the fourth-longest in NHL history. The Oilers (17-3-3) have won six straight.

stories.headline: Gauthier stretches goal streak to 10 games
stories.summary: Cutter Gauthier had a hat trick and an assist, but Anaheim lost 8-6 at St. Louis. He has 19 goals during the streak and is one shy of the NHL record for goals in a month. It's his fourth hat trick since Nov. 1, a first for any player in one calendar month.

stories.headline: Bedard leaves with injury as Blackhawks beat Leafs
stories.summary: Connor Bedard scored, then left early in the third period with an apparent shoulder injury in Chicago's 6-3 win. Coach Jeff Blashill said he'll have more tests, with an update expected Wednesday. Toronto has lost seven straight.

stories.headline: Heiskanen wins it in OT in his return
stories.summary: Miro Heiskanen scored at 3:36 of overtime as Dallas beat Vegas 4-3. Mikko Rantanen tied it with five seconds left in regulation and finished with a goal and three assists. Heiskanen had missed five games.

stories.headline: Schaefer's hat trick leads Islanders
stories.summary: Matthew Schaefer scored three times in a 5-1 win over Columbus, the first hat trick by an Islanders defenseman since Denis Potvin in 1982. The Blue Jackets have lost five straight.

standouts.name: Cutter Gauthier
standouts.note: Fourth hat trick since Nov. 1 in a losing effort.

standouts.name: Matthew Schaefer
standouts.note: First career hat trick in a 5-1 win over Columbus.

standouts.name: Darcy Kuemper
standouts.note: 40th career shutout ended a four-game Kings skid.

leagues.name: MLB
leagues.summary: Offseason · Bednar and Jeffers take qualifying offers; five others hit the market

stories.headline: Bednar, Jeffers accept qualifying offers; five decline
stories.summary: David Bednar stays with the Yankees and Ryan Jeffers with the Twins on one-year, $23.15M qualifying offers. Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki, Brandon Lowe, Trevor Rogers and Adrian Morejon declined and hit the market. Teams that sign them give up draft picks, with a possible lockout two weeks away.

stories.headline: Owners meet in New York as lockout nears
stories.summary: Owners meet through Thursday in what is likely their last in-person session before the CBA expires Dec. 1. The union rejected their Nov. 3 offer of a $258.2M salary cap starting in 2028. A lockout would most likely begin 12:01 a.m. ET Dec. 2, freezing signings and trades of 40-man players.

stories.headline: MLB takes salary cap pitch public
stories.summary: MLB released a five-minute video in which executive Morgan Sword makes the case for a cap and a payroll floor. Cubs pitcher Jameson Taillon criticized it. The video leaves out other proposed limits, including on the size and length of free-agent contracts.

stories.headline: Teams set 40-man rosters at Rule 5 deadline
stories.summary: Clubs added prospects to protect them from the Dec. 9 Rule 5 Draft. Detroit designated four players, including Matt Vierling, Jace Jung and Trey Sweeney; the Dodgers cut Jake Cousins and Christian Cairo. The non-tender deadline is Friday.
